strengths: Strong specific metrics throughout (~100 to 300+ users, tens of thousands of documents, three junior engineers mentored)
Excellent ATS keyword coverage for LLM/RAG roles - OpenAI, LangChain, Agents SDK, vector databases, embeddings all present
Honest acknowledgment of skill gaps in cover letter - explicitly names NLP and full-stack as growth areas
Opening hook in cover letter is genuine and specific - the pilot scaling story is memorable
Clean, scannable resume format with consistent structure
RAG and document intelligence focus is a differentiated specialization for enterprise AI roles
weaknesses: Company specificity is thin - 'AI-powered coaching' is mentioned but never explained or connected to candidate's retrieval expertise in a concrete way
Some cover letter phrases read as slightly generic: 'sits at the intersection I care about most,' 'tight collaboration between technical depth and user empathy'
TypeScript/full-stack listed in skills but not demonstrated anywhere in experience bullets - this creates a credibility gap
Resume is light on depth - only two positions shown, could benefit from more detail on technical implementation
revision_suggestions: Research Valence's product more deeply - what specific coaching use cases do they serve? What retrieval challenges does a coaching platform face? Connect your RAG experience to those specific problems.
Add 1-2 sentences about why AI coaching specifically matters to you, beyond the founding-team opportunity. Show you understand the product.
Either remove TypeScript from skills or add a brief bullet demonstrating full-stack work (even a side project or internal tool).
Replace generic phrases with more specific language: instead of 'sits at the intersection I care about most,' name the specific technical challenge that excites you.
Consider adding a Projects section to the resume if professional experience is limited - this could demonstrate broader technical range.
